• R&D Support: Demonstrate experience in supporting R&D initiatives as they relate to Clinical Site Payments business operations.

• Project Performance Monitoring: Assess project performance, monitor progress, identify and quantify variances, take necessary corrective actions, and communicate updates to stakeholders.

• Discrepancy Resolution: Work collaboratively with third-party site payment vendors to resolve payment discrepancies, historical issues, and fulfill monthly reporting requests.

• Payment Tracking: Track payments owed to clinical research sites per the negotiated unit price in each site’s contract.

• Invoice Management: Monitor invoice aging and outstanding payments in real time, adhering to established departmental and company guidelines.

• Risk Mitigation: Provide oversight on invoice and payment statuses, performing risk mitigation actions to proactively manage reviews, approvals, and payments.

• Risk Identification: Collaborate with management to identify risks, develop mitigation strategies, propose alternative solutions, and follow up on action items with cross-functional teams.

• Stakeholder Engagement: Maintain regular communication with external partners and investigators, as well as internal departments, regarding payment activities throughout the study lifecycle.

Business Acumen:

• Proven ability to prioritize multiple tasks, plan proactively, and achieve goals with moderate guidance.

• Strong project management and leadership skills with adaptability to meet deadlines and project requirements.

• Professional interaction with all organizational levels across functional areas and global regions.

• Capacity to complete tasks and projects with minimal supervision.

pharmaceutical industry

Excellent written and verbal communication skills and interpersonal relationship skills including relationship building and management skills.

title: Director, Legal Entity Planning & Forecast
description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

The Director, Legal Entity Planning & Forecasting will be a key member of the Corporate FP&A team and will own the enterprise legal entity forecasting and reporting framework. The role will translate the management forecast into a complete, accurate, and reconciled legal entity forecast. This serves as a key input to our corporate tax planning and transfer pricing processes, legal entity cash flow and liquidity forecasting, as well as other related accounting analyses. The position will partner with Corporate FP&A, Global Tax, Treasury, Accounting/Controllership, Finance Systems, and business finance teams across Commercial, R&D, Technical Operations, and G&A.

The successful candidate will combine strong FP&A and business planning capabilities with sufficient accounting, tax, intercompany, and legal entity knowledge to understand how management forecasts translate into legal entity financial statements and related implications on tax planning, transfer pricing, and capital allocation strategies (cash flow by entity perspective). This is a hands-on leadership role responsible for building governance, controls, and accountability around legal entity forecasting while ensuring one reconciled view of the company across management and statutory/tax needs.

The ideal candidate is proactive, highly analytical, comfortable operating in a dynamic global environment, and able to move between detailed model mechanics and executive-level insights. The role requires strong cross-functional influence, process design skills, and a continuous-improvement mindset.

Key Responsibilities:

•
Establish and govern the enterprise Legal Entity Forecasting framework, including process design, calendar, ownership, controls, data requirements, and reconciliation to the management forecast

•
Lead the translation of management forecasts into legal entity forecasts, ensuring entity-level P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow projections reconcile to the consolidated FP&A outlook

•
Partner with Finance Systems/TM1 to design scalable forecasting capabilities, enabling efficient capture and allocation of costs, intercompany activity, and other legal entity drivers across the enterprise

•
Provide reliable legal entity forecasts and insights to Global Tax to support tax provision, effective tax rate forecasting, tax planning, transfer pricing, impairment/valuation analysis, and other accounting-for-income-tax requirements

•
Partner with Treasury to assess legal entity liquidity and cash generation, identifying potential funding requirements, trapped cash, and implications for capital allocation and treasury risk

•
Perform regular actual-to-forecast and forecast-to-forecast variance analysis by legal entity, identifying key drivers, emerging risks, and potential implications for Global Tax, Treasury, Accounting, and management reporting

•
Establish governance and accountability across Legal Entity Finance Directors and functional teams, ensuring completeness, accuracy, timely submissions, and resolution of forecast risks

•
Provide management with actionable legal entity insights, highlighting forecast changes and emerging risks impacting GlobalTax, Treasury, Accounting, and enterprise financial planning.

Qualifications:

•
10+ years of progressive experience across FP&A, corporate finance, accounting, controllership, transaction advisory, audit, or related finance disciplines in a complex multinational environment.

•
CPA preferred. Big 4 audit, accounting advisory, transaction services, or similar background is highly valued but not required if equivalent corporate experience is demonstrated.

•
Demonstrated experience with legal entity forecasting statutory/entity-level planning, tax forecasting support, or integrated forecasting across FP&A, Global Tax, Treasury, and Accounting.

•
Strong understanding of US GAAP and consolidated financial statements; IFRS knowledge; knowledge of accounting for income taxes (ASC 740), impairment/valuation concepts, and the role of forecasts in external reporting.

•
Solid understanding of intercompany transactions, transfer pricing, and how operational activity flows through legal entities.

•
Experience with cash flow and liquidity forecasting and the ability to connect legal entity earnings, balance sheet movements, and cash requirements.

•
Experience in the pharmaceutical/biotechnology industry strongly preferred, with understanding of R&D, Technical Operations/manufacturing, Commercial, and Global Medical Affairs economics.

•
Public-company and multinational experience strongly preferred; SEC reporting exposure is a plus.

•
Advanced financial modeling and systems skills; TM1/Planning Analytics experience strongly preferred, with advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills.

•
People-management experience and demonstrated ability to influence across functions without direct authority.

•
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex entity-level financial information into clear executive insights.

•
Highly organized, detail-oriented, results-focused, and comfortable balancing strategic process design with hands-on execution.

The role focuses on scientific exchange, medical education, insight gathering, evidence generation support, and cross-functional collaboration to advance patient care and support organizational objectives.

The successful candidate is expected to maintain deep therapeutic area expertise in oncology, demonstrate strong scientific communication capabilities, and contribute strategically to medical affairs initiatives in Malaysia.

Main Responsibilities

1. Scientific Engagement and Partnership

•
Develop and maintain strong scientific relationships with oncologists, pathologists, researchers, and relevant healthcare stakeholders across Malaysia.

•
Conduct peer-to-peer scientific discussions on disease areas, clinical data, treatment landscapes, and BeOne Medicines products and pipeline.

•
Capture, synthesize, and communicate high-quality medical insights from external engagements to inform medical strategies, planning, and evidence needs.

•
Support medical projects, including early access programs, diagnostic pathway initiatives, and other patient-focused medical initiatives.

•
Maintain high standards of scientific credibility, professionalism, and ethical engagement in all external interactions.

2. Medical/Scientific Support and Education

•
Serve as a scientific expert and maintain current knowledge of clinical guidelines, competitor data, treatment pathways, and emerging evidence within oncology.

•
Support the planning and execution of medical education initiatives, scientific symposia, and advisory boards.

•
Deliver internal scientific training to support disease, product, data, and compliant communication knowledge.

•
Support the medical review and localization of scientific materials where appropriate.

•
Respond to unsolicited medical information requests with accurate, balanced, non-promotional information in accordance with approved processes and local requirements.

3. Evidence Generation and Research Support

•
Identify opportunities for local evidence generation, investigator-initiated studies (IIS), real-world evidence (RWE), registries, and collaborative research.

•
Support feasibility assessments and site identification for clinical trials and research initiatives.

•
Facilitate interactions between investigators and internal stakeholders.

•
Gather clinical insights and unmet medical needs to support medical strategy development.

•
Contribute to publication planning and scientific dissemination activities.

4. Cross-Functional Collaboration and Compliance

•
Collaborate closely with Market Access, Commercial, Regulatory, Pharmacovigilance, and Clinical Operations teams.

•
Contribute to annual medical planning and execution

•
Ensure all activities are conducted in compliance with company policies, local regulations, and applicable industry codes.

title: Senior Director, Organizational Change Management, Global Technology Solutions
description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

General Description:

As Senior Director, Organizational Change Management (OCM), you will lead GTS’s enterprise OCM strategy in support of the BeOne’s mission: helping BeOne build the next-generation global oncology company and expand access to high-quality cancer therapies worldwide. By proactively orchestrating organizational change, you will enable colleagues, customers, and patients to adopt intuitive experiences, scalable services, and capabilities delivered through a unified technology ecosystem.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Operational Strategy & Enablement, you will serve as GTS’s change architect and strategic advisor to executives and transformation sponsors. You will architect and orchestrate change across multiple regions, cultures, time zones, governance structures, and decision-making models, aligning diverse stakeholders around shared outcomes while adapting delivery approaches to local needs. You will shape strategy, portfolio sequencing, sponsorship, governance, and risk mitigation across GBS, ServiceNow, ERP, AI adoption, and operating model redesign, ensuring changes strengthen secure systems, compliant processes, trusted data, and AI-enabled intelligent automation.

You will scale a global OCM center of excellence and practitioner network, establishing methodologies, capabilities, and performance measures that accelerate adoption, organizational readiness, and measurable value. Through coaching and partnerships with the Global Technology Solutions Leadership Team (GTS-LT), Program and Portfolio Governance (PPG), Process and Service Excellence (PSE), Human Resources (HR), Corporate Communications, and business leaders, you will embed change leadership and the North Star outcomes into transformation delivery.

Essential Functions of the Job:

• Enterprise OCM Strategy & Governance: Define the GTS OCM vision, operating model, standards, and roadmap aligned with the North Star. Establish portfolio change criteria, assurance practices, and escalation mechanisms that strengthen adoption, value realization, security, compliance, and organizational readiness.

• Advisory & Sponsorship: Advise GTS leaders and sponsors on organizational impacts, stakeholder risks, alignment, and interventions. Coach leaders to visibly sponsor change and reinforce accountability.

• Transformation Portfolio Leadership: Oversee OCM across GBS, ServiceNow, ERP, AI, and operating model transformations. Integrate change requirements into portfolio planning, investments, governance, and the GTS Software Delivery Lifecycle to advance a unified technology ecosystem and scalable global capabilities.

• GBS & Operating Model Transformation: Partner with process owners and GBS leaders on transition strategies, workforce readiness, service adoption, and regional process standardization. Enable scalable services and intuitive experiences for BeOne colleagues while sustaining secure, compliant operations.

• OCM Center of Excellence: Lead a scalable global OCM capability encompassing methodologies, toolkits, quality standards, practitioner development, communities of practice, and champion networks.

• Adoption, Readiness & Value Realization: Establish measures for readiness, adoption, proficiency, user experience, and benefits realization. Apply trusted data, stakeholder feedback, and corrective actions to improve outcomes for colleagues, customers, and patients.

• Leadership Communications & Engagement: Shape transformation narratives and executive communications with Communications and business leaders. Oversee engagement for town halls, leadership forums, and GTS events.

• Talent & Team Leadership: Recruit, develop, and lead a global OCM team. Set objectives, allocate resources, manage partners, and build succession plans.

• North Star & OKRs: Translate the GTS North Star into actionable OCM priorities, outcomes, and OKRs. Strengthen accountability for intuitive user experiences, scalable services, unified technology, secure and compliant processes, trusted data, intelligent automation, and expanded access to cancer therapies.

Location:

• Preference for East Coast Location.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

• Lead a global OCM team, accountable for organization design, talent, performance, resources, succession, and external partners.

Required Education:

• Bachelor’s degree in Organizational Development, Business, Communications, Human Resources, Psychology, Engineering, or a related field required; a relevant Master’s degree is strongly preferred.

Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree or a Master’s degree (strongly preferred) in a related discipline with 12 + years of experience supporting enterprise transformation leadership.

• Change Management Certification: Prosci, Certified Change Management Professional (CCMP), or an equivalent advanced credential demonstrating recognized OCM expertise is strongly preferred.

• Transformation Credentials: Project Management Professional, Agile, Lean, or comparable certification supporting disciplined transformation planning, execution, and continuous improvement is preferred.

• AI & Digital Fluency: Demonstrates knowledge of enterprise artificial intelligence, digital adoption, intelligent automation, and technology-enabled change practices within complex organizations.

• Enterprise Leadership: 12+ years in organizational change, transformation, organizational development, or consulting, including 5+ years leading global teams or OCM functions.

• Large-Scale Transformation: Demonstrates success leading complex, multi-year transformations spanning technology, processes, operating models, workforce capabilities, organizational structures, and culture.

• Global & GBS Experience: Architects and orchestrates change across the Americas, Europe, and APAC, navigating cultural differences, regional contexts, and varied decision-making models.

• Executive Influence: Advises senior executives, aligns transformation sponsors, navigates organizational complexity, and influences strategic investment, prioritization, governance, and portfolio decisions.

• Life Sciences: Applies substantial experience within biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, or another highly regulated global environment requiring rigorous security and compliance.

• Enterprise Platforms: Leads organizational change and adoption across enterprise platforms including SAP, Workday, ServiceNow, Veeva, Ariba, and AI-enabled capabilities.

• People & Partner Leadership: Builds high-performing teams, develops talent, manages consulting partners, allocates resources effectively, and governs distributed delivery across regions.

Skills

• Enterprise Change Leadership: Expertise in ADKAR, CAP, Agile, Lean, human-centered design, and tailoring methods to context.

• Strategy & Business Acumen: Connects change to enterprise strategy, operating models, investments, risk, and business outcomes.

• Executive Presence & Influence: Credibility, judgment, and communication skills to advise and mobilize leaders across a global matrix.

• Organization & Talent Leadership: Designs capabilities, leads teams, coaches leaders, and builds sustainable change capacity.

• Communication & Facilitation: Exceptional writing, storytelling, negotiation, and facilitation skills; English proficiency at CEFR C1 or higher.

Computer Skills:

• Proficiency with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, and enterprise AI tools such as Copilot.

• Experience with Smartsheet, Miro, Visio, Canva, MindManager, or equivalent visualization tools preferred.

Other Qualifications:

• Business Acumen: Understands organizational drivers, financial performance, cross-functional workflows, market dynamics, and commercial outcomes influencing strategic priorities.

• Data-Driven & Process-Oriented: Applies analytical thinking, creative problem-solving, process discipline, and continuous improvement to strengthen operational performance.

• Proactive & Self-Directed: Independently advances priorities, anticipates challenges, organizes resources, and demonstrates initiative with limited oversight.

title: Global Regulatory Affairs (GRA) Fellow
description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

** When applying, please upload your curriculum vitae (CV), letter of intent, and unofficial college transcript in PDF format under the "CV/Resume" section of the application.

Education Required:

Candidate should have completed a Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD), Master’s in Regulatory Affairs, or a Ph.D. in life sciences by July 2027.

General Description:

The BeOne Medicines Global Regulatory Affairs (GRA) Fellow will engage in a one-year rotational program that includes working in various departments within GRA to support BeOne regulatory drug development in Global Regulatory Policy and Intelligence (GRPI), Regulatory Strategy, Advertising and Promotion, and Labeling. The Fellow will apply their scientific knowledge, regulatory learnings and independent judgment to support and execute key deliverables for each sub-function. These key deliverables, presentations and projects inform important regulatory strategy.  Effective communication, both written and verbal, and critical thinking are vital skills for this role. The fellowship will be conducted remotely beginning July 2027.

Essential Functions of the job:

The GRA Fellow will rotate throughout the Global Regulatory Affairs Department in the four below sub-departments and perform the tasks identified below under the supervision of each respective sub-department:

Global Regulatory Policy and Intelligence (GRPI)

•
The GRPI team analyzes and presents the latest in health authority regulatory trends, policy initiatives, and approvals across therapeutic areas.

•
The fellow will complete timely and thorough analyses of nuances of regulatory precedents along with tracking dynamic regulatory environment to support BeOne pipeline products.

•
Using critical analysis, problem-solving and writing skills, the fellow will work on GRPI deliverables (examples are regulatory background packages, competitive benchmarking summaries, regulatory strategy questions, and regulatory topic analyses, etc.).

•
Fellow will create presentations and present on relevant regulatory topics at internal forums.

•
Fellow will recruit and promote for potential future GRA fellowship recruitment cycle during their fellowship year.

Global Regulatory Affairs - Strategy

•
The regulatory strategy team plans and coordinates regulatory submissions and provides guidance to the cross-functional development teams on regulatory strategy and tactics.

•
The fellow will partner closely with the regulatory affairs strategy lead(s) by supporting the development and implementation strategies for optimal regulatory development of BeOne pipeline drug development programs.

•
Fellow will utilize GRPI deliverables to assess regulatory landscape to address regulatory challenges.

•
Fellow may support creation of important communications with health authorities including new INDs, cover letters describing the submission, and support NDAs/BLAs.

​

Global Regulatory Affairs - Advertising and Promotion

•
The regulatory advertising and promotion team administers the promotional review process, prepares FDA submissions for promotional materials, and provides regulatory review and oversight for promotional and non-promotional product communications.

•
The fellow will apply FDA regulatory requirements for promotion and other product related communications.

•
Fellow will actively participate in internal cross-functional Promotional Review Committee (PRC) Meetings.

•
Fellow will review promotional materials under supervision of regulatory advertisement and promotion staff member for new products and/or new indication launches.

​

Global Regulatory Affairs - Labeling

•
The labeling team develops and maintains global core labeling for commercial products and provides regulatory support for local labeling development and implementation.

•
The fellow will apply regulatory labeling strategies and operations, and support activities for management and governance of global and local product labeling.

•
Fellow will review and assess any developments (i.e., new indications, safety issues) and update/maintain global and local product labeling and Company Core Data Sheet (CCDS).

•
Analyzing labels (USPI and SmPC), the fellow will conduct labeling comparisons of potential new product and/or new indication launches.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

•
The position has no direct reports. The Fellow is part of a team that performs high quality and timely regulatory analyses. This position works closely with GRA as part of a matrix team.

Preferred Qualifications:

•
Professional work experience

•
Industry related experience

•
Leadership experience

•
Publications / Poster Presentations/Research

Other Qualifications:

•
Analytical and Critical Thinking: Strong problem-solving skills are essential to interpret complex regulations, assess their impact on organizational processes, and develop strategies to meet evolving regulatory demands.

•
Written and Verbal Communication Skills: Clear written and verbal communication is critical for drafting regulatory documents, explaining requirements to stakeholders, and liaising with regulatory authorities.

•
Project Management: Prioritizes work activities and uses time efficiently and completes tasks accurately. Follows instructions and responds to management direction.

•
Adaptability: The ability to stay updated on changing regulations, manage shifting priorities, and navigate ambiguity is vital in dynamic regulatory environments.

•
Innovation: The ability to creatively navigate regulatory constraints and propose forward-thinking solutions, such as leveraging emerging technologies or streamlining processes.

Computer Skills: Advanced application capability with Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and electronic document management system (i.e., Veeva).

title: Medical Affairs Fellow
description:

When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

** When applying, please upload your curriculum vitae (CV), letter of intent, and unofficial college transcript in PDF format under the "CV/Resume" section of the application. Please also have three (3) letters of recommendation emailed directly from your references to: medaffairsfellowship@beonemed.com.

Education Required:

Doctoral degree in Pharmacy (PharmD) from an accredited institution. Strong foundation in clinical pharmacy (completion of a residency, preferred).

General Description:

The US Medical Affairs Fellowship at BeOne Medicines is a 12-month postdoctoral training program designed to cultivate future leaders in the biopharmaceutical industry.

Reporting directly to the Executive Director, Disease Area Head of Solid Tumors in US Medical Affairs, the Medical Affairs Fellow is a key contributor within the US Medical Affairs organization, supporting the development and execution of strategic initiatives across solid tumor programs. In this role, the Fellow exercises independent judgment and discretion in analyzing scientific and clinical information, identifying data gaps, and developing solutions that inform medical strategy and stakeholder engagement.

Working in a matrixed environment, the Fellow collaborates with cross-functional teams to advance medical plans, support evidence generation initiatives, and deliver high-quality scientific communications. The Fellow is accountable for defined projects and deliverables that directly impact medical strategy, field engagement, and external scientific exchange.

This position is designed for doctoral-level scientists or clinicians seeking to apply their expertise in a dynamic, global oncology environment while contributing to the advancement of innovative therapies.

Essential Functions of the Job:

The Fellow will perform various tasks critical to Medical Affairs and BeOne business, which may include, but not limited to:

Medical Strategy & Planning:

• Lead defined components of US Medical Plans, including situation analysis, identification of strategic priorities, and development of tactical recommendations aligned with disease area objectives.

• Independently synthesize scientific, clinical, and competitive intelligence to inform medical strategy and lifecycle planning.

• Develop and maintain strategic metrics dashboards to evaluate execution effectiveness and identify areas for optimization.

• Provide strategic recommendations to cross-functional stakeholders based on data interpretation and insights.

Evidence Generation:

• Assess clinical and real-world evidence gaps and propose evidence generation initiatives to address unmet needs.

• Conduct scientific and feasibility reviews of Investigator-Initiated Trial (IIT) proposals, including evaluation of scientific merit, strategic alignment, and operational considerations.

• Analyze clinical and epidemiologic data to support publication planning and medical strategy decisions.

Scientific Communications & Publications:

• Develop high-impact scientific content, including advisory board materials, educational slide decks, and medical education resources.

• Translate complex clinical data into clear, scientifically accurate communications for internal and external stakeholders.

• Lead components of publication planning, including literature gap analyses, publication concepts, and abstract development.

• Serve as a scientific resource in the planning and execution of medical congress activities.

External Stakeholder Engagement:

• Plan and execute stakeholder engagement activities, including advisory boards and scientific meetings, ensuring alignment with medical strategy.

• Collaborate with Field Medical Directors to identify insights and translate field intelligence into actionable strategic recommendations.

• Develop engagement strategies for KOLs, investigators, and patient advocacy organizations to support medical objectives.

Medical Information & Reviews:

• Author scientific response documents (e.g., SRLs) using independent evaluation of literature and clinical data.

• Serve as a scientific reviewer in Medical and Promotional Review Committees (MRC/PRC), providing expert input to ensure accuracy, compliance, and scientific rigor.

• Evaluate medical information inquiries and determine appropriate scientific responses.

Leadership, Teaching, & Special Project:

• Provide mentorship and project oversight to US Medical Affairs Summer Interns, including project planning, feedback, and evaluation.

• Lead journal clubs, training sessions, or educational initiatives for internal teams.

• Independently design and execute a strategic capstone project that addresses a key business or medical need, presenting outcomes to senior leadership.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

Computer Skills:

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Outlook, Teams)

• Experience with scientific literature databases (e.g., PubMed, Embase)

• Ability to use digital tools for data analysis and project tracking

Required Qualifications:

• PharmD from an accredited institution

• Licensed pharmacist or recent pharmacy graduate with a clear intent to obtain licensure immediately post-graduation

• Strong understanding of clinical research methodology and demonstrated ability to independently analyze scientific data

• Self-motivated, ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, dynamic, matrixed environment

• Excellent organizational, communication (verbal and written), and interpersonal skills

• Embrace BeOne’s core values and competencies

• Eligible to work in the USA

Preferred:

• Experience in hematology/oncology research or clinical practice

• Prior experience in medical affairs, clinical research, or regulatory environments

Travel:

title: Associate Director, Commercial Master Data Management
description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

General Description:

The Global Commercial and Medical Affairs Technology team at BeOne is seeking an Associate Director, Commercial Master Data Management to support and lead the Ex-China Commercial Master Data Management (MDM) capability and drive operational excellence across commercial data platforms, customer data, analytics, and business applications.

This role serves as a business owner for commercial master data domains, governance processes, data quality standards, stewardship programs, and cross-functional data policies that enable trusted, compliant, and scalable data-driven decision-making.

This role partners closely with Commercial Operations, Marketing, Sales, Market Access, Patient Services, Analytics, Compliance, and Information Technology to ensure commercial data assets are governed, standardized, and optimized to support business objectives.

This role will establish the foundation for a customer-centric commercial data ecosystem by creating governance frameworks, stewardship processes, master data standards, and data quality programs across HCP, HCO, payer, patient, product, and organizational data domains.

Master Data Management

• Serve as hands-on business owner and architect for commercial master data domains, including HCP, HCO, payer, customer, product, and organizational hierarchies.

• Build and maintain enterprise master data standards, business rules, hierarchies, and data ownership models.

• Establish and run the Commercial Data Stewardship Program.

• Develop and execute master data lifecycle processes, including onboarding, enrichment, maintenance, validation, and retirement.

• Build and fine tune match rules, merge rules, and survivorship logic; perform customer matching, deduplication, affiliation management, and hierarchy maintenance directly to produce trusted “golden records.”

• Configure and maintain customer communication preferences, consent management processes, and related compliance requirements.

• Ensure MDM technologies and platforms align with commercial business requirements and configure them to meet those needs.

• Identify and implement opportunities to improve operational efficiency through data standardization and automation.

• Support enterprise initiatives involving AI, advanced analytics, customer engagement, and commercial transformation.

Data Quality & Stewardship

• Build commercial data quality standards, KPIs, and monitoring processes, and run them on an ongoing basis.

• Develop scorecards and reporting that provide visibility into data health across commercial domains.

• Perform root-cause analysis and execute remediation for recurring data quality issues – writing the fixes, not just assigning them.

• Partner with business stakeholders to prioritize and resolve data-related risks and opportunities.

• Drive continuous improvement initiatives that measurably increase trust in commercial data assets.

Commercial Data Operations & Business Enablement

• Write and maintain operational support processes, documentation, SOPs, data dictionaries, and process maps to improve platform sustainability and supportability.

• Translate business requirements into working technical solutions, and build the datasets, validations, and outputs directly; support user training, documentation, and adoption efforts.

• Deliver and validate high-quality commercial master data provisioning across Account Planning, CRM, Customer Master, Business Intelligence, and Commercial Analytics platforms, ensuring data consistency, governance, and alignment with business requirements.

• Partner with business stakeholders to identify opportunities for process improvements, workflow automation, and operational efficiencies.

• Monitor operational metrics, data quality indicators, and platform usage, and personally implement continuous improvements.

Commercial Applications Data Platform Management

• Run day-to-day operations, enhancements, and support activities for commercial technology platforms including Customer Master Data and related data solutions.

• Coordinate and perform platform releases, upgrades, enhancements, and defect resolution activities.

• Support commercial product launches and business initiatives by preparing data, ensuring technology readiness, and testing data availability.

• Conduct impact assessments and hands-on cross-functional reviews for system changes, integrations, and new data sources.

• Partner with business and technology stakeholders to prioritize enhancements and build improved platform capabilities.

Data Integration & Analytics

• Partner with Data Engineering and Enterprise Architecture teams and build data integration and provisioning across commercial systems.

• Build and coordinate integration activities between CRM, Customer Master, Marketing, Analytics, and Enterprise Data Warehouse platforms.

• Write SQL and support the development and maintenance of semantic layers, reporting datasets, and business intelligence solutions.

• Collaborate directly with Analytics and AI teams to improve data quality and support advanced reporting and analytical use cases.

• Monitor and troubleshoot data pipelines and integrations to ensure reliable and timely data delivery.

• Implement automated validation rules, matching logic, and data hygiene scripts to eliminate duplicate entries and maintain database integrity.

Vendor & Offshore Team Management

• Coordinate delivery activities across offshore development teams, managed service providers, and technology vendors, working hands-on in testing and validating deliverables.

• Manage project execution, testing, deployments, and production support activities across internal and external teams.

• Monitor vendor performance against established service levels and support continuous improvement initiatives.

• Review vendor output, reproduce and diagnose issues, and facilitate root-cause analysis and operational reviews for commercial systems and data platforms.

• Support release planning, environment management, documentation, and knowledge transfer activities.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

• None currently, possible in the future.

Education Required:

• Bachelor’s  in Computer Science, or a related field.

Required Qualifications:

Technical Expertise:

• Bachelor's Degree with 8+ years of experience / Master's in Computer Science or related field with 6+ years of experience.

• 8+ years of Pharmaceutical industry Commercial operations or related experience architecting and building Enterprise Data Management platforms, with direct hands-on delivery.

• Hands-on experience implementing & managing Master Data Management solutions is a must.

• Demonstrated ability to personally write and tune match rules, merge rules, and survivorship logic to produce “golden records” across Capability, Consent, Payer, Patient, HCP/HCO domains.

• Familiarity with master data management platforms and commercial data architectures or comparable products.

• Hands-on knowledge of commercial data mastering, including identity resolution, hierarchy and relationship management, consent management, data governance, data quality monitoring, and integration across HCP, HCO, payer, patient, consent, and product systems.

• Strong hands-on SQL and experience working with Cloud based platforms and technology solutions is a must (AWS Redshift, EC2, Databricks, Snowflake, Reltio etc).

• Hands-on experience with MedPro & OneKey data is a must. Ultmarc data experience is nice to have.

• Excellent written / verbal communication skills and presentation and project management skills.

• Ability to coordinate needs assessments across the commercial & other business organizations, and an ability to build and deliver a comprehensive solution to those needs.

• Demonstrated ability to work well within a matrixed environment, and an ability to build solid relationships / make connections across the organization.

• Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills and solid business acumen with the ability to manage and provision large amounts of data to enable business analysis with high level of performance and trust.

• Must be able to identify operational weakness and personally implement corrective action / plan.

• Proven ability to grow and develop others.

Business Acumen & Leadership:

• Strong collaboration skills with stakeholders, and cross-functional teams.

• Experience leading Operational/analytics initiatives that drive measurable business impact.

• Excellent communication and storytelling skills, making insights accessible and actionable for executives.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience in pharmaceutical or healthcare industry.

• Exposure to commercial, medical, or patient data ecosystems.

• Hands-on experience with commercial data providers including SP/SD, IQVIA, Symphony Health, Komodo, Definitive Healthcare, Veeva Open Data, and similar sources.

Travel:

title: Manager, Safety Scientist
description:
BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

PLEASE SUBMIT ALL RESUMES/CV'S IN ENGLISH FOR CONSIDERATION

Language Requirement: Fluent English is Required

Preferred Experience: Pharmaceutical/Biotech Industry

Location: Brazil Remote

General Description:

The Manager, Safety Scientist supports assigned compounds in conjunction with Product Safety Leads (PSLs) to conduct signal detection, evaluation of safety data, assessment of safety risks, responses to regulatory inquiries, and regulatory-required periodic reporting. In this role, you will apply effective prioritization, critical thinking, and judgment-based decision making to execute these key deliverables in compliance with global regulations and internal processes. Effective communication and influence with internal and external stakeholders is an important capability for this role. This role represents GPS Safety Science internally and externally at a global level and functions as an authoritative and professional member of relevant teams.

Essential Functions:

Signal and Safety Data Evaluation

• Support the identification, analysis, and evaluation of safety data for signal detection from all applicable sources

• Perform signal detection and signal assessment along with required documentation following BeiGene process

• Support and propose data acquisition strategy, methodology, and approach for safety evaluations

• Support analysis of safety data and author safety assessment

• Collaborate with PSLs, scientists, pharmacoepidemiologists, and other cross-functional personnel as appropriate to ensure thorough evaluation and aggregate analysis of safety data, demonstrating the ability to understand and communicate scientific issues and strategy

• Execute signal assessment analysis per strategy and assist with the preparation of presentations for Safety Management Team and Company Safety Committee

• Support the preparation and presentation of safety data at safety governance meetings (Safety Management Team and Company Safety Committee) and for Safety Monitoring Committee (SMC), Data Monitoring Committee (DMC)/Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB)

• Apply judgment-based decision-making principles to contribute to key scientific/clinical discussions

• Apply effective communication skills to lead and facilitate safety team meetings

• Communicate relevant safety information to core team, business partners, and key stakeholders in a timely manner

• Support the development, update, and review of safety communication documents (e.g., Dear Investigator Letter, Informed Consent Form, Investigator’s Brochure, Healthcare Professional communications [DHCP letter or DHPC], Labelling documents, Risk Management Plan, etc.) in collaboration with Safety Science team members and relevant cross-functional team members

Clinical Trial Support

• Support the review of safety data and monitor the safety of patients on allocated clinical trials

• Support the writing and review safety sections and provide safety expertise for development of Protocols, IBs, ICFs, Safety Analysis Plans (SAPs), Tables Figures and Listings (TFLs), Medical Monitoring Plans, CSRs (incl. China ADR Summary) and other relevant project/study documents and answer ad-hoc safety queries from ethics committees

• Contribute to safety sections and review aggregate reports, e.g., PBRERs, DSURs, PADERs

• Support the authoring and review of safety sections of regulatory submissions, e.g., IND/CTA (General Investigational Plans, China Risk Control Plans), NDA/MAA (SCS/ISS, RMPs, initial Package Inserts) collaborating with PSLs and other Clinical Study Team (CST) members

• Support the authoring of Storyboards and Briefing Books for HA interactions

• Support ad-hoc review of the Safety Management Plans

• Support investigator training

Risk Assessment, Regulatory Inquiries, and Periodic Reporting

• Assist with analysis of safety data and author relevant safety sections of global regulatory inquiries and periodic reports including Development Safety Update Reports (DSURs), Periodic Adverse Drug Experience Report (PADER)/Periodic Adverse Experience Report (PAER), Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs), Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Reports (PBRERs), and Risk Management Plans (RMPs)

• Provide high quality support for additional evaluation requests from health authorities (e.g., PRAC PSUSA) for assigned compounds

• Support strategy development, analysis, and response to safety questions from health authorities, IRBs/ECs.

• Assist with integrated Benefit/Risk assessments

Promote and Advance the Field of Pharmacovigilance

• Any other tasks assigned by manager to assist in departmental activities

Minimum Requirements – Education and Experience:

PharmD, RN or PhD/ MS in a medical field or biological science and 2+ years as a Safety (Pharmacovigilance) Scientist.

Other Experience:

• Pharmaceutical product development experience

• Experienced in global regulatory requirements for pharmacovigilance

Supervisory Responsibilities:

The position has no direct reports. The Manager, Safety Scientist is part of a team that performs high quality and timely scientific and operational safety analysis. This position works closely with the Safety Scientist group as part of a matrix team to conduct safety assessment and safety risk management activities per BeiGene process and applicable regulations.

Travel:  Less than 10%

Computer Skills:

• Knowledge working with a safety database (i.e., Argus) for retrieval of safety information

• Intermediate knowledge of MedDRA and signal management system

• Advanced application capability with Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and electronic document management system (i.e., Veeva)

• Familiarity with data mining tools and analyses tools such as Spotfire and PowerBI
